qt: to the Commission Hanna Gedin (The Left), Jonas Sjöstedt (The Left) Subject:

A recent investigation1 raises serious concerns that private communications belonging to EU citizens, scanned under the EU’s temporary derogation from the ePrivacy Directive (Chat Control 1.02), may be analysed using software developed by the US company Palantir. According to the investigation, reports submitted by technology companies to the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) are processed using Palantir’s Foundry platform. NCMEC has reportedly confirmed that Foundry is used for all reports handled through its CyberTipline. This raises questions about the handling, security and potential secondary use of sensitive personal data. 1.
Can the Commission confirm whether private communications scanned under Chat Control 1.0 are processed using Palantir’s Foundry software?
If so, what measures has the Commission taken to ensure that Palantir cannot access, retain, share or use this data for purposes other than combating child sexual abuse?

Can the Commission unequivocally guarantee that Palantir does not, under any circumstances, have access to or process private communications belonging to EU citizens that do not contain child sexual abuse material, including communications incorrectly flagged by automated detection systems?

https://arvidgrange.substack.com/p/investigation-eu-citizens-private. Regulation (EU) 2026/1881 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 July 2026 on a temporary derogation from certain provisions of Directive 2002/58/EC as regards the use of technologies by providers of number-independent interpersonal communications services for the processing of personal and other data for the purpose of combating online child sexual abuse (OJ L, 2026/1881, 28.7.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1881/oj). 1 2
